title.official: Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct for Organizations Developing Advanced AI Systems
title.short: G7 Hiroshima AI Process Code of Conduct

relevance.reason: A voluntary G7 code of conduct addressed to organisations developing the most advanced AI systems, including foundation models and generative AI. It is a leading non-binding implementation instrument and builds on the OECD AI Principles. It is not a treaty and creates no legal obligation.
ai_provisions: Whole document — risk identification and mitigation across the AI lifecycle; transparency; security; incident reporting; content authentication; research investment; governance
Preamble — voluntary guidance; living document; applies to advanced AI systems including foundation models and generative AI
relevance.excluded_scope: Voluntary and addressed to organisations, not States; no enforcement, conformity assessment or market-access consequences.

dates.notes: Issued as part of the Hiroshima AI Process and welcomed in the G7 Leaders' Statement of 30 October 2023.

status_note: Adopted and published as a voluntary code. No signature or ratification; organisations may endorse it and report under the separate Hiroshima Process Reporting Framework.

languages.note: English text acquired. The Japanese government publishes Japanese materials; the English text is the version acquired and analysed. No authentic-language clause exists because the instrument is not a treaty.
